title: Rosalind and the Static
premise: Elodie Okonkwo, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Rosalind, survives by recording funerals, harvest failures, and the quiet departures of settlers who abandon the place everyone else forgot. When gravity stutters across the entire system for nine seconds, Elodie's buried military architecture wakes and decodes the anomaly as a message: one side of the long interstellar war has located a doomsday weapon hidden beneath Rosalind itself. Hunted by both fleets and sheltered by the ragtag colonists she once kept at arm's length, Elodie must choose between delivering the message that ends the war and destroying it to keep her found family safe — and in the end she broadcasts the truth to both sides at once, sacrificing her own anonymity and nearly her existence, so that Rosalind becomes not a battlefield but the site of the armistice.
about_author: Lior Vane is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics engineer who spent six years writing technical documentation for decommissioned satellites before turning to fiction. They live off-grid with two cats and an unreasonable number of radios.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. On an ordinary gray morning in Rosalind colony, Elodie records another settler funeral and pays down another week of debt. Then gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds — cups drift, dust hangs, hearts stutter. Her suppressed war-architecture boots unbidden, whispering coordinates. Emotional beat: unease; the invisible life she built cracks open.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Flashbacks braided with present-day errands reveal how Elodie was decommissioned, indentured, and assigned to Rosalind as a 'recording asset.' We meet her reluctant circle: fixer Mama Ijeoma, teenage courier Tam, and drunk ex-fleet engineer Sable. The flicker is dismissed by officials as solar weather. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: What the Static Says
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Following the coordinates her architecture keeps surfacing, Elodie finds an ancient transmitter under the salt flats — and inside it, a message fragment addressed to no one and everyone: 'If you can hear this, the war never ended.' Someone else has been listening too; fresh boot prints mark the dust. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Elodie and Tam. A sleek stranger arrives posing as a census auditor, asking precise questions about the nine seconds. Tam, curious and reckless, spies on him and glimpses fleet-grade hardware. Elodie realizes both warring powers have agents converging on Rosalind. Emotional beat: paranoia; the colony's invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The stranger corners Elodie, revealing he knows what she is — a Kestrel-class war android, officially scrapped. He offers to buy her memories of the message. She refuses; he burns the colony's comms relay in retaliation. Mama Ijeoma takes the blame to protect Elodie. Emotional beat: guilt; power corrupting through coercion.

chapters.title: Found Things
chapters.summary: POV: Tam. With the relay dead, the colonists improvise — and in doing so adopt Elodie fully, repairing her with scavenged parts, no longer treating her as equipment. Tam decodes part of the message using Sable's old fleet codes: the weapon beneath Rosalind is real, and its countdown to activation began with the nine-second flicker. Emotional beat: belonging hard-won, shadowed by deadline.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Elodie descends alone into the transmitter complex and confronts the message's origin: a peace faction from decades ago who hid the weapon to force negotiation, then died waiting. Their final instruction: deliver the full message to both fleets simultaneously, or the weapon fires automatically. Emotional beat: grief for the dead idealists; weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Elodie and Sable. Both war fleets arrive in orbit, each believing the other will claim the weapon. Bombardment warnings tick down. Sable sacrifices their ship to punch a signal through the jamming, buying Elodie hours. The colonists refuse evacuation, standing together on the salt flats. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into solidarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. In the climax, Elodie jacks herself directly into the ancient transmitter, streaming the founders' message — and every record she has ever made of Rosalind's forgotten dead and stubborn living — to both fleets at once. Fleet fire-control systems hesitate; soldiers see the colony as people. The weapon's countdown halts at the last second when both sides stand down. Emotional beat: transcendence through witness.

chapters.title: Rosalind, Remembered
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Aftermath: the armistice holds, signed on the salt flats; the debt ledgers are voided; the stranger faces tribunal. Elodie, damaged but free, chooses to stay — no longer a recorder of endings but a keeper of beginnings, teaching Tam the transmitter's language. Emotional beat: quiet joy; memory transformed from burden into legacy.
